To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) attention is a sequence to sequence learning problem, and that (b) the posterior attention models outperform the prior attention models in the context of neural machine translation and abstractive summarization.

(i) we introduce a posterior attention model for sequence to sequence learning; (ii) we show that posterior attention is more robust to noise and better generalizes to longer sequences; and (iii) we provide an analysis of attention in sequence-to-sequence tasks and show how posterior attention can better model the dependence between the attention and output sequences.

1) attention models that are widely used today are not adequate for modeling the dependencies between attention and output tokens, and 2) we propose posterior attention as a new attention model that is able to capture these dependencies and is able to outperform the current state of the art on the WMT'16 En-De translation task.

In this paper, we show that the current state-of-the-art sequence-to-sequence models for speech recognition do not adequately model dependencies among the attention and the output tokens across a sequence.
In the context of a neural network, a recurrent neural network (RNN) is a type of neural network where the output from one layer is fed into the input of the next layer.
the attention mechanism in sequence-to-sequence models is a useful tool, which can be improved by using a better attention mechanism, but is not necessary to achieve the same results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to model the dependence among attention and output tokens in a sequence-to-sequence model and how this dependence can be used to improve sequence generation.
we propose a new attention model for neural sequence to sequence models that is able to capture this inter-token dependence.
we propose to model the attention and output sequences jointly, using a single neural network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
attention is a multi-headed mechanism that should be applied to all tokens in a sequence, rather than just the current token.
the attention and output sequences can be modeled in a joint manner, and that doing so leads to better performance.
the attention mechanism should be modeled as an autoregressive sequence to sequence (Seq2Seq) model.
